mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in FEDFUNDS above 3% for two consecutive months predicts a near-term positive S&P 500 20-day forward return due to expectations of accommodative monetary policy and reduced risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 3% and remains >3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-positive despite sustained FEDFUNDS >3% for >2 months, or inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises >2% over the same horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS accompanied by a decline in UNRATE over the next month signals labor market strengthening without wage inflation, which is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases in the following month
regime_hint: labor market improving but wage growth contained
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative when PAYEMS up and UNRATE up, or the correlation between PAYEMS and UNRATE is not negative over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in GDPC1 (real GDP) followed by a subsequent rise in HOUST (retail sales) predicts positive S&P 500 20-day returns as it reflects strong consumer and business demand.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases in month t and HOUST increases in month t+1
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite the sequential increases in GDPC1 and HOUST, or the lagged correlation is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) below its 50th percentile for three months predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as it signals supply-side weakness and potential recession risk.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 50th percentile for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive when INDPRO is below 50th percentile for >3 months, or the signal is not statistically significant in walk-forward tests.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains persistently below 1% for four consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to continued tight monetary policy and reduced market liquidity.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS <1% for >4 months, or the effect is not statistically detectable.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 3% combined with a decline in PAYEMS suggests weak labor demand and increased unemployment risk, leading to negative S&P 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3% and PAYEMS decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive when UNRATE <3% and PAYEMS down, or the interaction is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in both GDPC1 and RSAFS (retail sales) predict a positive S&P 500 20-day return as it reflects sustained economic momentum and consumer confidence.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 up and RSAFS up in the same month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive when both proxies show upward momentum, or the interaction is not predictive.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in UNRATE above 4% in a month is associated with negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns due to expectations of tighter labor markets and potential wage pressures that suppress equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4% in the current month
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive when UNRATE >4%, or the effect is not statistically significant in out-of-sample tests.
